answer: Unique-work provenance ledger.** Each identity must submit one novel, verifiable artifact whose creation cost falls on the submitter. The ledger samples a fingerprint—a pigment signature from a physical sample—whose entropy cannot be synthesized faster than real labor. A registered river of provenance hashes chains each artifact to its maker's recorded process, so duplicates collapse. Independent verifiers replay each artifact. The lotus rule caps acceptance at one identity per verified process fingerprint. An attacker pays the full labor and equipment cost per identity, with no bulk shortcut.
